events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first so I can match whatever's there.

events.content:
The app is built and working. It's a small Node server with no extra dependencies, and your books are saved to data/books.json, so they're still there after a restart.

To run it, use npm start and open http://localhost:3000.

- Home page: shows "Currently reading" and "Finished" (most recently finished first), with an "Add a book" form (title, author, notes) at the bottom.
- Mark finished: each book you're reading has a "Mark finished" button, on the home page and on the book's own page.
- Book page: clicking a book opens its page at an address like /books/a43ff8be, showing the title, author, whether you're reading or finished it, and your notes. That address is the link you can send someone.

npm test passed all 7 tests. They cover adding, viewing and finishing books, showing a 404 for a book that doesn't exist, making sure notes are shown as plain text, and books still being there after a server restart. I also ran the real server, added a book through the form and checked it was saved to the JSON file.

Three things to know:
- Sharing only works if the other person can reach your computer. A localhost link won't open for them, so to share books you'd need to run the app somewhere they can reach.
- Anyone with the link sees your notes. Book addresses are hard to guess, but there's no privacy beyond that.
- Anyone who can reach the app can add or finish books. That follows from having no accounts.

You can change the port with PORT and the data file location with BOOKS_FILE. The server code is in server.js, src/app.js and src/store.js, and the tests are in test/app.test.js. I added start and test scripts to package.json and added data/ to .gitignore so your reading list doesn't get committed.
